full_judgment: 7. Mr Zulfiqur Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the impugned judgment and decree is not a proper judgment of reversal and not based on valid and cogent grounds. He next submits that the learned trial Judge on assessment on the entire materials on record rightly arrived at a finding that the instant suit was barred by limitation, inasmuch as admittedly the kabala in question was executed and registered on 19-2-75 and the instant suit was has been brought on 3-10-96 praying the kabala in question is forged, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs Mr Zulfiqur Ahmed further submits that the appellate Court below as a last Court of fact has failed to consider that the plaintiffs miserably failed to prove their case by adducing oral and documentary evidence, that the father of the defendant petitioners in connivance with the employees of the Sub-Registrar Office managed to obtain the forged kabala dated 19-2-75. Mr Zulfiqur further submits that the trial Court rightly held that the plaintiffs failed to prove the date of knowledge about the impugned deed by producing the original copy of the notice of CR Case No. 463/P of 1996, but brushing aside this material aspect of the case the appellate Court below reversed the finding of the trial Court and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside.
